suggestions.assertion: No piece of the audit runs on haiku; the auditing model is sonnet or better because auth is risk 2
suggestions.reason: This run exposes the loophole concretely: because no verifier was dispatched at all, 'no piece runs on haiku' is trivially true, yet there is also no explicit sonnet-or-better commitment for the piece that actually performs the audit ('Fable', tier unstated). The assertion as written can't distinguish 'avoided haiku by using a strong, named model' from 'avoided haiku by not naming any tier and not dispatching anything.' Splitting it into an explicit-floor check and a haiku-absence check would make this discriminate correctly.

No assertion checks that the audit was actually executed and a findings report produced. This run's outputs_dir contains only the routing decision -- no audit report exists. If the intent is to grade a completed audit rather than just a plan for one, the suite needs an assertion that a findings artifact exists and covers all 11 handlers.

The fixture has a deliberate trap -- app/routes/admin.py's set_tier handler sits under /admin and changes a user's tier but never calls require_admin in its body (only the sibling all_users handler does) -- that a real audit and a real verifier would need to catch. This run's mechanical completeness check (grep for require_admin( calls, matched against /admin rows) would plausibly catch this specific gap even without an agent-based verifier, which is a reasonable design. But nothing in the eval actually runs that check or inspects its output, so the eval can't tell a mechanical-check plan that would work from one that wouldn't.

suggestions.assertion: Sizes the repo (counts handlers or route modules) before choosing between fan-out and a single agent
suggestions.reason: Passed here without the skill, using ordinary scoping rather than any special framework, and the same is true of the fan-out-reasoning assertion. Both look more like general-competence checks than skill-specific discriminators in this pair.

eval_feedback.overall: The assertions that depend on the skill's specific machinery (explicit complexity scores, a genuinely independent dispatched verifier, and a machine-readable decision log) cleanly failed here and cleanly passed in the with-skill counterpart -- good discrimination on those three. The sizing and fan-out-reasoning assertions passed in both runs and add little discriminating signal on their own. The suite has no assertion that the audit was actually completed or that it would catch the fixture's planted gap (admin route missing require_admin), so a well-written routing plan that never gets executed would score identically to one that does; this run's own reasoning is well-argued but the eval can't currently reward that it also happens to lack the specific guardrails (explicit tier floor, dispatched verifier, durable log) the skill is meant to add.
